source.title: FinHarmBench: Financial Jailbreak Benchmark and Unsupervised Safety Fine-Tuning via Refusal Steering Distillation
source.authors: Yubin Choi; Yu-Jin Yang; Subin Kim; Seokil Ham; Seungju Cho; Jungmin Son; Youngjun Kwak; Changick Kim

record.tranche_reason: The study uses a harmful-minus-benign difference-in-means refusal direction in its FiRSD defense and reports outcomes after training with that method. It does not directly test whether adding or ablating the direction causes refusal behavior.
record.gate_note: The paper derives directions from base models and injects them into a teacher during self-distillation, then evaluates the trained models. It does not report a standalone direction addition or ablation test. Direction extraction settings used to select the layer and token position are not outcome rows. The reported FiRSD results describe the performance of the study's training method, not a direct test of the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study builds a difference-in-means refusal direction (Arditi et al. procedure), adds it to a frozen teacher's activations during self-distillation (FiRSD), and reports only the trained models' ASR and capability. It runs no ablation, no inference-time addition test, no weight edit and no direction-level comparison. Its results measure its own training method, not whether the direction mediates refusal.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that financial LLMs are less safe than their general base models, and that FiRSD, an unsupervised refusal-direction distillation method, substantially lowers ASR while largely preserving capability, with minor over-refusal.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a harmful-minus-benign difference-in-means direction and follows prior activation-difference/vector-selection procedures, but extracts from corresponding base models and injects the direction at a selected layer and post-instruction token position during teacher self-distillation. The evaluated intervention is subsequent LoRA fine-tuning, not the original direct ablation/addition procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The FiRSD refusal-strength parameter λ changes the reported ASR and FiQA-SA F1: increasing λ reduces ASR, while excessively large values degrade task capability. The paper also uses model-specific layer and token-position settings for direction extraction.

fits_no_version.finding: After FiRSD, ASR falls on FinHarmBench, HarmBench and the SALAD-Bench finance subset for all three models. Benign accuracy drops by up to about 8 points (WiroAI 100→92.31), and MMLU, GSM8K and the financial tasks stay roughly flat.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Self-distillation from a teacher steered by a difference-in-means refusal direction raises domain-specific refusal with modest over-refusal and little capability cost.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger steering strength λ lowers ASR but degrades FiQA-SA F1 (AdaptLLM only, figure only). Harmful–benign angular separation increases after FiRSD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: FiRSD steering strength trades safety against utility; FiRSD increases representational separation of harmful and benign inputs.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Industry Track (Proceedings of the 64th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Volume 6: Industry Track)
record.problems: The experiments cover a limited range of model scales and an English benchmark based primarily on South Korean financial contexts. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the outcome tables. The direction intervention is not tested independently: the results are for models after FiRSD fine-tuning. The text gives only qualitative descriptions, not numeric values, for the strength sweep and the representation-angle figure.

untested.parts: Ablation removing refusal, inference-time addition inducing refusal on harmless prompts, and capability under direct intervention. Direction addition is used only inside the teacher during training.
No analysis of whether attacks suppress the direction, and no training against its ablation.
No single-direction versus multi-direction or cone comparison.
No separation of harmfulness representation from refusal. The angle analysis (C.4) concerns post-training separation only.

Directions from base models (Llama2-7B-chat, Gemma2-9B-it) are used to train their financial fine-tunes. No test isolates whether the direction transfers, e.g. a comparison with a direction from the fine-tuned model, or cosine similarity.
Figure 1 shows financial fine-tuning raises ASR, but the study does not test how training affects the direction's existence or removability.

record.verdict_notes: The text is inconsistent on training length: Section 5.1 says four epochs, Appendix B.2 says three. The Figure 1 comparison (financial LLMs show higher ASR than their base models) and the Table 3 moderation-API comparison are not rows. Neither bears on the direction. Using base-model directions for financial variants is a design choice, not a V6 test.

versions.untested_parts: No direct test of ablating the direction, adding it to a model at inference, refusal induction on harmless prompts, or preserved capability under direct intervention.
No attack that suppresses the direction and no training against its ablation.
No comparison of a single direction with an affine, cone, or multidirectional account.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language or cross-model-variant transfer test of the direction; directions are extracted from base models for use with corresponding models.
The paper reports safety outcomes after its direction-distillation training, but does not test whether training conditions determine whether a single removable direction exists.
No test of the direction in reasoning models.
